title: Olist Support Agent
summary: A support desk that routes fictional order requests and gates simulated refunds with policy and review.
outcome: Let reviewers trace an order request from customer intent to an exact, auditable simulated action.
sourceNote: Source reviewed from the project worktree.
lead: An order support desk that uses a model to propose a route and puts refund decisions behind policy, review and customer confirmation.
challenge: A support request can describe a delivery question, a damaged order, or a refund without using those labels. The desk needs to interpret the request while keeping authority to issue a refund separate.

flow.detail: The hosted demo accepts built-in fictional requests and uses Nemotron to propose an intent route.
Application policy combines the route with scoped order and delivery facts to determine the next step.
Where required, a separate reviewer assesses the proposal. The customer confirms the specific action and amount.
The controlled workflow guards the PostgreSQL write and uses idempotency to avoid duplicate simulated refund receipts.

decisions.decision: Use the model for routing and keep action rules in application code.
decisions.tradeoff: Unclear requests can be handed back for review. Supported actions and acceptable evidence have to be defined in advance.

decisions.decision: Bind review and confirmation to an exact action.
decisions.tradeoff: Changes to the action or amount require fresh confirmation, keeping approval tied to what the customer sees.

limits: The Azure demo uses built-in fictional orders. Recorded refund receipts represent simulated actions without payment settlement.
diagramAlt: Fictional requests are routed by Nemotron. Policy and scoped facts determine whether review and confirmation can lead to a simulated receipt.
diagramCaption: The model proposes a route. Policy and confirmation gate the simulated write.
